parts.zh: W: 今天的特别嘉宾是布莱克威尔勋爵
W: 我们的听众一定会非常想了解外交部门的职业生涯
M: 恐怕除了我们都在新闻中看到的内容之外
M: 不过请放心，我们驻那里的领事馆中的专家特使会密切关注事态发展
W: 那么，一个人要怎样才能从事外交事务呢？
M: 可以选择的道路有很多
W: 您认为从事这份工作需要哪些关键技能？
M：我还没说完。等我们完成后把它提交上去
段的牢骚，且女方在 the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 反而说董事会几乎一致支持；把这话安到女方说 toug

items.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

choices.text: He has distinguished himself in foreign service.
choices.zh: 他在外交服务领域表现出色。

choices.text: He is his country's ambassador to Winopia.
choices.zh: 他是他的国家驻Winopia的大使。

choices.text: He is currently an electrical engineer.
choices.zh: 他目前是一名电气工程师。

choices.text: He craves attention from the media.
choices.zh: 他渴望得到媒体的关注。

items.stem: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?

choices.text: A government reshuffle.
choices.zh: 政府改组。

choices.text: A fundamental reform.
choices.zh: 根本性改革。

choices.text: Some sort of political reorientation.
choices.zh: 某种政治重新定向。

choices.text: Some sort of crisis of legitimacy.
choices.zh: 某种合法性危机。

items.stem: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?

choices.text: All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell.
choices.zh: 所有外交官都有或多或少相似的故事可讲。

choices.text: It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy.
choices.zh: 获得一些外交实践经验是先决条件。

choices.text: Different people can take different paths.
choices.zh: 不同的人可以走不同的道路。

choices.text: It is a must to first obtain a law degree.
choices.zh: 首先必须获得法律学位。

items.stem: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?

choices.text: Key skills required of a diplomat.
choices.zh: 外交官所需的关键技能。

choices.text: The making of an expert diplomat.
choices.zh: 如何成为一名专业外交官。

choices.text: Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric.
choices.zh: 外交话语和修辞。

choices.text: Contributions by diplomatic envoys.
choices.zh: 外交使节的贡献。

items.stem: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?

choices.text: They have got their work done.
choices.zh: 他们已经完成了工作。

choices.text: They both look tired
choices.zh: 他们两人看起来都很累。

choices.text: They can meet again tomorrow anyway.
choices.zh: 反正他们明天还能再见面。

choices.text: They are both anxious to go home.
choices.zh: 他们都急着想回家。

items.stem: What does the woman say is a little tough?

choices.text: The board members' insufficient support.
choices.zh: 董事会成员的支持不足。

choices.text: Two months devoted to the same contract.
choices.zh: 两个月都投入在同一份合同上。

choices.text: Working two months without any progress.
choices.zh: 工作两个月却没有任何进展。

choices.text: The man's long concentration on the project.
choices.zh: 男士长时间专注于这个项目。

items.stem: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they'll finish by next week?

choices.text: Unprofessional.
choices.zh: 不专业的。

choices.text: Inspirational.
choices.zh: 鼓舞人心的。

choices.text: Exceptional.
choices.zh: 杰出的。

choices.text: Delusional.
choices.zh: 妄想的。

items.stem: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?

choices.text: Fewer rectifications of the contract.
choices.zh: 减少对合同的修改。

choices.text: More support from the board members.
choices.zh: 得到董事会成员更多的支持。

choices.text: The early implementation of the project.
choices.zh: 项目的提前实施。

choices.text: The alignment of all sections of the contract.
choices.zh: 合同所有部分的一致。

items.stem: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?

choices.text: When two employees propose contrary solutions to their dispute.
choices.zh: 当两名员工针对他们的争议提出相反的解决方案时。

choices.text: When two employees are directed by their respective manager.
choices.zh: 当两名员工分别由各自的经理指导时。

choices.text: When two people behave in an apparently clashing manner.
choices.zh: 当两个人的行为方式明显相互冲突时。

choices.text: When two people tell different stories of the same event.
choices.zh: 当两个人对同一事件讲述不同的故事时。

items.stem: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?

choices.text: How it got resolved.
choices.zh: 它是如何得到解决的。

choices.text: How it happened.
choices.zh: 它是如何发生的。

choices.text: What it was about.
choices.zh: 它是关于什么的。

choices.text: When it was settled.
choices.zh: 它是何时解决的。

items.stem: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?

choices.text: They intervened promptly lest their dispute escalate.
choices.zh: 他们迅速介入,以免争议升级。

choices.text: They tried to ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
choices.zh: 他们试图查明事情的实际真相。

choices.text: They assumed the best about them and moved on.
choices.zh: 他们对他们做了最好的假设并继续前行。

choices.text: They persuaded them to put their conflict aside.
choices.zh: 他们说服他们将冲突放在一边。

items.stem: What do an increasing number of Americans do according to the passage?

choices.text: Dine out daily.
choices.zh: 每天外出就餐。

choices.text: Budget sensibly.
choices.zh: 理性预算。

choices.text: Enjoy cooking.
choices.zh: 享受烹饪。

choices.text: Shop at groceries.
choices.zh: 在杂货店购物。

items.stem: What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to?

choices.text: Shopping.
choices.zh: 购物。

choices.text: Sewing.
choices.zh: 缝纫。

choices.text: Entertaining oneself.
choices.zh: 自我娱乐。

choices.text: Fashion designing.
choices.zh: 时装设计。

items.stem: What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch?

choices.text: Satisfy their taste.
choices.zh: 满足他们的口味。

choices.text: Cut down expenses.
choices.zh: 减少开支。

choices.text: Eat more healthily.
choices.zh: 吃得更健康。

choices.text: Cultivate new hobbies.
choices.zh: 培养新爱好。

items.stem: What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America's grocery industry?

choices.text: People's intense focus on convenience.
choices.zh: 人们对便利性的强烈关注。

choices.text: People's deteriorating family finances.
choices.zh: 人们不断恶化的家庭财务状况。

choices.text: People's strong aversion to junk foods.
choices.zh: 人们对垃圾食品的强烈厌恶。

choices.text: People's increasing dislike of cooking.
choices.zh: 人们对烹饪日益增长的厌恶。

items.stem: What is the number-one reason a bag ends up lost according to this talk?

choices.text: Its owner's flight is delayed because of bad weather.
choices.zh: 其主人的航班因恶劣天气而延误。

choices.text: Airlines cannot find its owner without an ID tag on it.
choices.zh: 航空公司因行李箱上没有身份标签而无法找到其主人。

choices.text: Airline staff have not correctly coded its destination tag.
choices.zh: 航空公司工作人员没有正确编码其目的地标签。

choices.text: Its owner has forgot to pick it up from the baggage claim.
choices.zh: 其主人忘记从行李提取处取走它。

items.stem: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems?

choices.text: Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt.
choices.zh: 其标签可能在传送带上被撕掉。

choices.text: Its tag may get stuck in the sorting machine.
choices.zh: 其标签可能卡在分拣机里。

choices.text: It may be sent to a wrong destination.
choices.zh: 它可能被送到错误的目的地。

choices.text: It may be picked up by someone else.
choices.zh: 它可能被其他人取走。

items.stem: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?

choices.text: Purchase irretrievably lost things at auction.
choices.zh: 在拍卖会上购买无法找回的丢失物品。

choices.text: Contact the airport staff to find our missing bag.
choices.zh: 联系机场工作人员寻找我们丢失的行李。

choices.text: Get the airline agent's phone number before boarding.
choices.zh: 登机前获取航空公司代理人的电话号码。

choices.text: Avoid packing valuable items in our checked baggage.
choices.zh: 避免在托运行李中打包贵重物品。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about using one's smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?

choices.text: It can be behaviorally hazardous.
choices.zh: 这在行为上可能是有害的。

choices.text: It can be especially disappointing.
choices.zh: 这可能特别令人失望。

choices.text: It can be socially harmful.
choices.zh: 这在社交上可能是有害的。

choices.text: It can be really embarrassing.
choices.zh: 这可能真的很令人尴尬。

items.stem: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?

choices.text: They considered it inevitable.
choices.zh: 他们认为这是不可避免的。

choices.text: They held a negative view towards it.
choices.zh: 他们对此持负面看法。

choices.text: They were concerned with its effects.
choices.zh: 他们担心其影响。

choices.text: They saw it as a sign of social evolution.
choices.zh: 他们将其视为社会进化的标志。

items.stem: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?

choices.text: Elaborate forms of social contact.
choices.zh: 复杂形式的社交接触。

choices.text: Ill effects on one's sense of pride.
choices.zh: 对个人自尊感的不良影响。

choices.text: Poor relationships with others.
choices.zh: 与他人的不良关系。

choices.text: Vicious cycles of detachment.
choices.zh: 疏离的恶性循环。

items.stem: What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?

choices.text: The ill treatment they get as tourists.
choices.zh: 他们作为游客受到的不良待遇。

choices.text: The nonprofessional business they see.
choices.zh: 他们看到的不专业的商业行为。

choices.text: The impersonal accommodations.
choices.zh: 缺乏人情味的住宿条件。

choices.text: The many adventures on their way.
choices.zh: 旅途中的诸多冒险经历。

items.stem: What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements?

choices.text: They have been the classic way to visit Europe.
choices.zh: 它们一直是游览欧洲的经典方式。

choices.text: They attract tourists with location and decoration.
choices.zh: 它们以地理位置和装饰吸引游客。

choices.text: They have long been competing with chain hotels.
choices.zh: 它们长期以来一直在与连锁酒店竞争。

choices.text: They are in fact a completely new idea in America.
choices.zh: 它们实际上在美国是一个全新的概念。

items.stem: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?

choices.text: Your financial status.
choices.zh: 你的财务状况。

choices.text: Your family's consent.
choices.zh: 你家人的同意。

choices.text: Your property.
choices.zh: 你的房产。

choices.text: Your personality.
choices.zh: 你的个性。

items.stem: What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about?

choices.text: Costs for starting the business.
choices.zh: 创业的成本。

choices.text: The number of guests to receive.
choices.zh: 接待客人的数量。

choices.text: The facilities to provide.
choices.zh: 提供的设施。

choices.text: Opportunities for income.
choices.zh: 收入机会。
